name: Blind Portrait

scoring.report_note: Report pair-level deltas only. Never rank individuals — the exercise measures the pair's communication loop, not personal talent.

description: Two-minute pre/post measure for the Blind Portrait communication exercise. Scores at pair level: how did instruction-giving, listening and assumption-checking change between round A (no questions) and round B (three questions)?

instructions.pre: Before pairing up. Each participant answers alone, about their own last week at work — not about the exercise.
instructions.post: Immediately after the debrief. Same items, now answered about the exercise just completed, as a pair.

items.pre_text: When I give instructions, I check what the listener already assumes.
items.post_text: During the exercise, we checked what the other assumed before starting.

items.pre_text: When I am unsure, I ask rather than guess.
items.post_text: When the drawer was unsure in round B, we asked rather than guessed.

items.pre_text: I send instructions into silence and find out later what was understood.
items.post_text: In round A, we sent information into silence and saw the result on paper.

items.pre_text: I adapt how I explain based on who is listening.
items.post_text: As describer in round B, we changed our explanation because of who was drawing.

items.pre_text: When a misunderstanding surfaces, I go back and fix the instruction, not the person.
items.post_text: When the gap surfaced at the reveal, we fixed the describing, not the drawer.

items.pre_text: I can tell the difference between 'I explained it' and 'they understood it'.
items.post_text: The two drawings showed the difference between explaining and understanding.

report.title: Blind Portrait — pair communication delta
sections: Round A vs round B judge-card scores
One suggested repair habit per pair, derived from the largest positive delta
